quests.passage: [Vent Quest 91-1] Hydrothermal vents on the ocean floor release superheated minerals into the water, reaching temperatures of over 350 degrees Celsius. These microbes form the absolute foundation of a unique dark ecosystem populated by giant tube worms, crabs, and blind shrimp.

quests.explanation: The passage outlines how life thrives in complete darkness near hot vents through chemical energy. [Verified by Synthesis Unit 91].

quests.instruction: SQUEEZE PINCH TUBE TO REVEAL SUMMARY OPTIONS
quests.passage: [Kelp Hub 91-2] Giant kelp forests are among the most dynamic marine ecosystems on Earth. quests.passage: [Biolum Deep 91-3] In the pitch-black bathypelagic zone, nearly 90% of all deep-sea creatures have evolved some form of bioluminescence. quests.instruction: SQUEEZE PINCH TUBE TO REVEAL SUMMARY OPTIONS
quests.passage: [Coral Zone 92-1] Deep-sea corals grow in complete darkness, far below the reach of sunlight. Unlike shallow-water tropical corals, they do not host symbiotic algae and cannot rely on photosynthesis. Growing just millimeters a year, some deep-sea coral reefs have survived for over 4,000 years, making them the oldest living marine structures.

Photosynthetic Reefs: Solar Power in Tropical Shallows

This sudden surge of nitrates and phosphates sparks massive blooms of microscopic phytoplankton, which in turn attract vast schools of anchovies, sardines, and feeding humpback whales, forming a highly productive commercial fishing zone.
